# CHANGELOG-PENDING

Unreleased changes to be curated into the next `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

**Instructions for contributors:** add a one-line entry under the appropriate section when your PR introduces a user-visible change. PR number in brackets at the end. Entries are curated (not auto-generated) before each release.

Format: `- Brief description of what changed. ([#NNN])`

---

## Added

<!-- feat() PRs go here -->
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): `install --resume-thread <uuid>` continues an existing Codex conversation (saved under `--codex-home`'s `sessions/`, as `codex resume <id>` takes it) in the owner's DM with the agent; it is resumed once, the first owner task in the DM, and every other room starts a new thread. An id with no saved conversation is refused before the token is read or anything is written. ([#6387])
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): `install` and `connect` take `--resume-session <uuid>` to host an existing Claude Code conversation instead of a new one. The id must name a transcript under the config dir's `projects/` that no running Claude Code process has open; otherwise nothing changes and connect's code is not spent. A kept id is replaced under the same proven-gone rule as `--new-session`; when it is not, the agent stays installed under the kept id and the command exits 79.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local, codex-local): `install --agent <Matrix ID> --token-stdin` takes the agent's relay token pasted at a hidden prompt (or one piped line): the bare `<relay_url>|<secret>` token or a `REMOTE_TASK_TOKEN=` / `AG2_REMOTE_TOKEN='…'` line. It is written to the agent's seat as `connect` writes it (mode 600, never through a link), then install runs as with `--token-env-file`; the other adapter already serving the agent, or the agent's job still running, is refused before the token is read. ([#6263])
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local, codex-local): several agents per host, one job per agent. An agent installed on its own root runs as `ai.ag2.sparrow.<adapter>.<agent key>` (systemd `ag2-sparrow-<adapter>.<agent key>.service`), the key being its readable root segment, with its own bridge job, its config under `~/.config/ag2-sparrow/agents/<agent key>/`, claude-local's tmux socket in a short `~/.config/ag2-sparrow/run/<digest>/`, and its operation lock at `~/.config/ag2-sparrow/locks/<job>.oplock`, which nothing removes; `uninstall` removes the agent and run dirs once only its own files are left. `verify`, `uninstall`, `attach`, `stop` and `debug-run` take one selector (`--agent <Matrix ID>`, `--key <agent key>`, `--work <dir>` or `--single`), needed only when several jobs are installed; `install` checks one it is given; new `list` shows each job with its selector, and every command a line prints carries the selector that names exactly that job. A job an earlier release installed keeps its fixed name and is verified, reinstalled and removed as before. A job whose config is gone is recovered only from its own marked bridge unit or the declaration beside the root its unit records, and only when that declaration's agent is the one its root names (the bridge runtime's own rule); a declaration that cannot be read or proven the job's makes uninstall refuse and name its manual `rm`. The repair a line prints, `install <selector>`, reuses the job's recorded token file and flags, rewrites a config that no longer loads, and mints a new session id for a malformed one; an install's bridge starts only once its session holds the root, and is left stopped when it never does. A repair reads and runs nothing recorded until the record is proven that job's on its own root; every install, connect and uninstall of an agent, on either adapter, holds the agent's fence (`~/.config/ag2-sparrow/locks/agent.<agent key>.fence`) through the settle of the session it started; a failed install that leaves the session not running stops the agent's bridge too; printed `rm` lines are shell-quoted. One agent is still one bridge across adapters.
- Wedge probes: `src/wedge_probes.py` gives the shared wedge detector three pure signatures for the core seat (a live core with no ready task watcher and no standby, a `core-status.json` stuck on one step, and a prompt or sign-in only a person can clear), with the reason and what unblocks it. It publishes nothing itself; `report()` is the one hand-off to the detector. health-check's core-proactive-loop and core-supervisor rows now use the same rules.
- ag2-sparrow: `ag2-sparrow-hatch no-reply <result_file> [--reason TEXT]` ends a task with nothing posted and waits until Sparrow has settled it with the gateway (exit 0 settled, 1 not, 3 queued but not confirmed), and each owner task file says to end a task that needs no reply with a `[no-send]` result. ([#6128])
- ag2-sparrow: opt-in AgentActivity task lifecycle. `REMOTE_TASK_LIFECYCLE_V2=1` sends the lease `worker_id` and `execution_generation` on ack and results, beats each task on `/v1/tasks/heartbeat`, stops the core when the broker cancels or reclaims an attempt (withdrawn when a newer generation is acked here first; a newer attempt it stopped anyway is posted as failed); a task the broker closes, or cancels before the ack, leaves the inbox if the core has not taken it up, and the core is stopped if it has, and reconciles with `/v1/tasks/active`. An attempt nobody will answer stops beating and is posted as failed: its task file left the queue unanswered for 10 min (never dropped from flight as completed elsewhere), or the core took the queued file up and then wrote no turn activity or result for 30 min while the core is not mid-turn (2 h when its state is unknown). `REMOTE_TASK_TURN_CONTEXT=1` adds per-attempt turn files and gates each result on the turn's room actions. Both default off. ([#5883])
- ag2-sparrow: with `REMOTE_TASK_TURN_CONTEXT=1`, a task the owner answered resumes as a new turn carrying the answer as quoted room data, once per question episode, and each task file tells the agent to ask a blocking question with `room.question.ask` on its task id, sending any visible text with `room.message.send` first (its result file is not posted while the question is open). A wake's task file says it is a new turn of the task and must end with its own result. For a wake turn only (its file carries a `wake_episode:` header), the Stop hook does not count a result older than the queued file as its answer, and a turn that recorded a turn-ledger no-send loses the in-progress exemption, so the wake it left unanswered blocks; every other task is judged as before. A woken attempt is judged answered only by its own result, not the first attempt's archived reply, so a wake stopped or closed before the core takes it is withdrawn and a lost wake is failed. A question about the owner's own errand is asked in their DM, not a shared room, and a turn whose question's outcome was lost posts `waiting_input`, never its "I asked" note as the reply. The bridge's attempt records move to one ledger, `state/relay-task-ledger.json`: each broker effect (ack, result, cancel-ack) is claimed there before it is sent and committed after, and each newer generation or wake runs as a run of its own with its own result item, including a generation served after the earlier one finished (its answer refused as stale, say), which is held for its ack rather than taken for a redelivery. Its task file says whether the earlier attempt's answer was delivered, so the core answers again when it was not. The earlier `relay-task-attempts*.json` is ignored, so attempts in flight when the bridge is upgraded are not resumed. ([#5885])
- agent-activity: with `SUTANDO_STOP_INTERRUPT=1` (off by default; also the manifest's config), a Stop interrupts the core's running turn with one Escape when that turn is on exactly the stopped task, so a long tool call or a terminal prompt no longer delays the stop. The turn comes from Claude Code's own turn hooks (`UserPromptSubmit`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`): the tasks its prompt named and the dialog it is parked on. The key is fenced on that turn in the pane. A turn on several tasks, on another task, on no task, or one that cannot be read gets no key, and the Stop stays cooperative. The task shows `stop requested` until the stop is ruled: CANCELLED when the core answered the control task and wrote no result, left to delivery when it wrote a ready one (the shared readiness rules, a wake turn's own only), CANCELLED after an hour unanswered. The ruling survives restarts. Only a stop from the bridge's own control writer or the owner's local voice session (owner tier, in headers no body can forge) stops anything. A stop for a task a pool worker holds is routed to that worker's inbox, so the worker's own watcher interrupts and rules it, and the switch reaches each worker's watcher. Skills take a Stop through the new manifest field `on_stop_requested`; with none taking it (the switch off), a cancel marks the task CANCELLED at once, as before. With the switch on, a task the engine fails as stalled also gets a cooperative stop instruction. Cancel instructions and the agent-activity hook handle a gateway instance's `task-<instance>~task-<id>` as one id. ([#6089])
- ag2-sparrow: with `REMOTE_TASK_TURN_CONTEXT=1`, a task that asks this agent a room question carries the question as quoted, secret-redacted room data, and owner tasks are told to answer it once with `room.question.answer`, deciding from what `room.question.inspect` returns. The turn gate ignores outcomes about another task, so answering never parks or closes the agent's own task. An answer is matched to its question in the journal; a question answered here, or whose answer cannot be told, is never offered again, and the record of it is kept until the question expires. ([#6092])

## Fixed

<!-- fix() PRs go here -->
- ag2-sparrow: the bridge's `poll network error` and `poll recovered` lines add how much of a poll gap the host was awake (`868s since last successful poll, 35s of it awake`) when it slept through part of it, so a sleeping Mac no longer reads as a poll hung for minutes. An awake gap logs as before. ([#6439])
- ag2-sparrow: a withheld non-owner result whose private review DM answers HTTP 403 "sender is not in this room" is settled after that one send (still withheld from the shared room, its review record kept, the refusal logged) instead of being re-sent on every 1 s scan. The refusing room is dropped from the review-room cache, so the next withheld result reaches the owner in a new private room. Any other 403 is retried as before. ([#5054])
- ag2-sparrow: a relay ask that repeats an earlier one from the same person in the same room folds into it (`[deduped:]`) instead of being reported as "The holder's delivery destination or sender could not be verified". The bridge writes the ask's `asked_by` above `task:`, and `asked_by` joins the task header vocabulary. A fold between different askers or rooms, or of an ask with no room, is still refused.
- worker-pool: a pool worker that has its own agent sends its proactive notes (for example the owner line after a room join) as that agent, from its own lane, into that agent's owner DM: `result_publish.py` stamps a worker session's proactive file `proactive-<ts>.by-<worker>.txt`, only that worker's lane claims it, and no core lane or other bridge does. The worker seat's `s-space` MCP proxy mints from the worker's own vault credential through `scripts/connections.py worker-mcp-credential` (`AG2_MCP_WORKER_CREDENTIAL`), never the core's; a worker with no enabled identity of its own keeps acting through the core in both.
- Tests: a test that runs an agent with `SUTANDO_TEST_MODE=1` (the spawned voice-agent suites, for one) no longer shows real desktop notifications on the machine running it. The notify helper (`src/platform.ts` and its Python twin `src/sutando_platform.py`) writes the banner to stderr instead of calling osascript, PowerShell or notify-send. Production, which never sets the variable, is unchanged. ([#6219])
- Voice: after a region refusal, voice comes back as soon as the network route is fixed. Retry on the error card (or the mic button) asks Google again and connects on that attempt, instead of showing the earlier refusal again, and a client that stays connected is redialed on the normal schedule (1 s, rising to 60 s) instead of waiting 5 minutes. While Google still refuses, the region message is shown as before. Other terminal failures (credits, quota, key, model) keep the 5-minute hold. ([#6218])
- Voice: when Google refuses Gemini Live because of the network's region (close 1007, "User location is not supported", common behind a VPN that exits in Hong Kong or mainland China), voice says the region is refused, that text chat still works, and how to route `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` through a supported region, instead of reporting the model as unavailable. Agent state carries the new reason `location-unsupported` (category `network`). ([#6217])
- tmux probe (core and ag2-sparrow): the liveness probe and the tasks-active check find tmux at its usual install locations when it is not on PATH, as under launchd, instead of reporting the core as down. ([#6131])
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): new `install --allow-collaborator` (persisted, shown by `verify`, off by default) submits an attested collaborator's task (team tier, `collaborator: true`) into the session with the shared non-owner note, as the relay loop and the routine and cloud-session adapters gate it. `--allow-non-owner` no longer covers collaborators: an install that served them through it refuses them until reinstalled with `--allow-collaborator`. The collaborator is served in the owner's session, not on an isolated turn. ([#6195])
- worker-pool: the remedy timer keeps the launcher's `SUTANDO_STOP_INTERRUPT` (including the `0` opt-out) in its LaunchAgent, so a worker it relaunches keeps the Stop setting. A spawner with a different value reinstalls the timer once; one without the setting, or an explicit install without it, keeps the saved value. ([#6186])
- ag2-sparrow: the Hatch hook's timed steps now fit its 30 s script timeout (12 + 4 + 4 s, each with a 1 s kill grace), a step whose child ignores SIGTERM is killed, and no child the hook starts keeps holding its poll lock. ([#6184])
- Task watcher: a session watcher whose inbox is outside its workspace (an inherited `SUTANDO_WORKSPACE_DIR`, as a test run on a live host has) no longer overwrites the workspace's sentinel while that workspace's own watcher is live, nor removes it on exit. Such a run made the core's live watcher read as not ready for minutes, and the Stop hook then blocked until a re-arm. The standby-gate test now isolates its workspace.
- ag2-sparrow: a bridge running with `REMOTE_TASK_LIFECYCLE_V2` off no longer retires a queued wake run (`task-…~~N`) left by a V2 run as already answered because its task's first result was delivered. The run stays for the core: a `[no-send]` answer closes its task, and a text answer is quarantined to `undelivered/` for review rather than lost. ([#6166])
- ag2-sparrow (behind `REMOTE_TASK_LIFECYCLE_V2`): a held serve's saved copy is redacted before it is written. Its body, the wake's answers and the room question no longer keep a pasted token or `vault set` value on disk, and the run published from it is not intercepted a second time; a held copy never stores an owner's `vault set` (the owner is told to resend it). The ledger becomes format 5 on its first write: rolling back to an earlier Sparrow leaves its bridge unable to read the ledger, so it holds every task rather than save a raw copy; set the ledger aside to start clean. ([#6135])
- ag2-sparrow (behind `REMOTE_TASK_LIFECYCLE_V2`): closing a turn already closed no longer logs `Permission denied` on its `.closed` file, and an ack that another post of the same claim already recorded no longer logs `ack for a serve this attempt no longer holds`. ([#6139])
- agent-activity: the room's live status shows what the agent is doing ("Working: Running tests") instead of only "Thinking…". A tool call with no step line writes its rules phase word as the task's working row in its room, when the room does not already show that phase; a call with a step line writes only that line, as before. Never step text in a phase row, and nothing for a task without a room. ([#6146])
- ag2-sparrow (behind `REMOTE_TASK_LIFECYCLE_V2` / `REMOTE_TASK_TURN_CONTEXT`): the four task-lifecycle failure schedules from #5885's review are closed. A ledger read that fails or finds a damaged map is unknown, never a decision; each held serve keeps its own saved copy, so no generation publishes another's; a wake served again under a new lease is held and decided by its ack; an open ack claim alone recovers a lost ack. The ledger becomes format 4 on its first write: on a host that opted in, rolling back to an earlier Sparrow leaves its bridge unable to read the ledger, so the attempts in it are not resumed; set the ledger aside to start clean. ([#6088])
- task-orphan-check: a task's age is how long it has waited in this inbox (its `local_time:` header), not since the sender sent it, so messages held at the broker while the app was closed are answered on relaunch instead of archived as orphans. Only a `local_time:` above `task:` counts, so a body line cannot make a fresh task from an older writer look orphaned. ([#5929])

## Changed

<!-- refactor(), perf(), docs() changes visible to operators go here -->
- macOS notifications are off by default. Sutando posts no macOS desktop notification (pending questions, bridge restarts, health checks, the agent shepherd, voice offline/online, context drop, screen recording) unless `sutando.config.local.json` sets `"notifications": {"macos": true}`. The same alerts still reach the owner's DM or the core's task queue. There is no exception: the gateway bridge's no-workspace alert, which has no DM to fall back on, is silent too unless you opt in. Windows and Linux notifications are unchanged.
